subject: chemistry

items.q: What does oxidation mean in terms of electrons?
items.correct: Loss of electrons (OIL RIG: Oxidation Is Loss).
items.misconception: Only the gaining of oxygen, nothing else.
items.why: Oxidation Is Loss, Reduction Is Gain of electrons; gaining oxygen is just one example of oxidation.

items.q: What does iron need in order to rust?
items.why: Rusting needs oxygen and water together; salt speeds it up.

items.q: In electrolysis, where do positive ions move?
items.misconception: To the positive electrode, because they are positive.
items.random_wrong: They don't move; electrolysis works on solids.
items.why: Opposite charges attract, so positive cations go to the negative cathode; the compound must be molten or dissolved.

specSource: CCEA GCSE Chemistry (2017) specification; Redox, Rusting & Iron
